# RQ:

Does a high carbon tax rate lead to lower GHG emissions per capita after factoring in fossil fuel share in the energy mix and GDP?

### packages installed:

install.packages("tidyverse") install.packages("tinytex") install.packages("hrbrthemes") install.packages("ggrepel")

```{r}
#| label: Setup and packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tidy: true

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(ggrepel)


Carbon_tax <- read_excel(
  "Carbon_tax.xlsx", sheet = "Compliance_Price", skip = 1)
GHG <- read_csv("GHG.csv")
Population <- read_csv("Population.csv")
GDP <- read_csv("GDP.csv")
Energy_mix <- read_csv("Energy_mix.csv")

```

(Tax rate is USD per tonne of CO2-equivalent)

```{r}
#| label: Cleaning data sets
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#Choosing and renaming relevant columns
My_countries <- c("Austria", "Belgium", "Denmark", "Estonia", "Finland", 
                  "France", "Germany", "Greece", "Hungary", "Iceland", 
                  "Ireland", "Italy", "Latvia", "Lithuania", "Luxembourg", 
                  "Netherlands", "Norway", "Poland", "Portugal", 
                  "Slovenia", "Spain", "Sweden")
  
Year_range <- 2005:2024

Carbon_tax_clean <- Carbon_tax %>%
  filter(
    `Instrument Type` == "Carbon tax"
    ) %>% #filtering out ETS only keeping carbon tax
  mutate(
    Country = str_extract(`Name of the initiative`,
  paste(My_countries, collapse = "|"))
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Country)) %>%
  select(
    Country, all_of(as.character(Year_range))
    ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Country, names_to = "Year", values_to = "Tax_rate_usd"
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.numeric(Year),
    Tax_rate_usd = ifelse(is.na(Tax_rate_usd), 0, Tax_rate_usd)
    )

no_tax_countries <- setdiff(My_countries, unique(Carbon_tax_clean$Country))

no_tax_filled <- expand_grid(Country = no_tax_countries, Year = Year_range
    ) %>%
  mutate(Tax_rate_usd = 0)

Carbon_tax_clean <- bind_rows(Carbon_tax_clean, no_tax_filled) %>%
  arrange(Country, Year)

#Choosing and renaming relevant columns
GHG_clean <- GHG %>%
  select(
    `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE
    ) %>%
  rename(
    Country = `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, 
    Year = TIME_PERIOD, 
    Total_emissions = OBS_VALUE
  )

#Choosing and renaming relevant columns
Population_clean <- Population %>%
  select(
    `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE
  ) %>%
  rename(Country = `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, 
         Year = TIME_PERIOD, 
         Population = OBS_VALUE
         )
#Choosing and renaming relevant columns
GDP_clean <- GDP %>%
  select(
    `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Country = `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`, 
    Year = TIME_PERIOD, 
    GDP_per_capita = OBS_VALUE
  )

#Choosing and renaming relevant columns
Energy_mix_clean <- Energy_mix %>%
  select(
    Country = `Geopolitical entity (reporting)`,
    Year = TIME_PERIOD, 
    Source = `Standard international energy product classification (SIEC)`, 
    OBS_VALUE
  ) %>%
  filter(Source %in% c("Solid fossil fuels", 
  "Natural gas", 
  "Oil and petroleum products (excluding biofuel portion)", "Total")
         ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Source, values_from = OBS_VALUE, values_fill = 0 
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    Fossil_fuels_share = (`Solid fossil fuels` + `Natural gas` +
    `Oil and petroleum products (excluding biofuel portion)`) 
    / Total * 100
    ) %>%
  select(
    Country, Year, Fossil_fuels_share
    )
```

```{r}
#| label: Merging data sets
#| echo: true

Merged1 <- merge(
  Carbon_tax_clean, GHG_clean, 
  by.x = c("Country","Year"), by.y = c("Country", "Year")
  )

Merged2 <- merge(
  Population_clean, GDP_clean, 
  by.x = c("Country","Year"), by.y = c("Country", "Year")
  )

Merged3 <- merge(
  Merged1, Merged2, 
  by.x = c("Country","Year"), by.y = c("Country", "Year")
  )

Trial_dataset <- merge(
  Merged3, Energy_mix_clean, 
  by.x = c("Country","Year"), by.y = c("Country", "Year")
  )

```

### Calculating: emissions per capita = Total emissions/ Total population (Emissions per capita is measured in tonnes of CO2-equivalent per person)

Unit of measure is in tonnes

```{r}

Trial_dataset$Emissions_per_capita <- 
  Trial_dataset$Total_emissions * 1000000 / Trial_dataset$Population 

Final_dataset <- Trial_dataset %>%
  select(
    Country, Year, Tax_rate_usd, GDP_per_capita, Fossil_fuels_share, 
    Emissions_per_capita
  )
```

Plotting each countrie GHG emissions per capita throughout the years. How did emissions evolve throughout the years?

```{r}
#| label: GHG emissions per capita
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 8

ggplot(
  Final_dataset, aes(x = Year, y = Emissions_per_capita, color = Country)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2005, 2024, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "GHG emissions per capita", y = "GHG emissions (tonnes CO2 per person)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)


```

```{r}
#| label: Carbon tax rates throughout the years
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 6

Final_dataset %>%
   mutate(
    Carbon_Tax = ifelse(Tax_rate_usd <= 0, NA, Tax_rate_usd),
    Country = fct_reorder(Country, Tax_rate_usd, .fun = max)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Year, Country, fill = Carbon_Tax)) + 
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2005, 2024, by = 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm")
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
    breaks = c(5, 25, 50, 100, 150),
    na.value = "white",
    name = "Tax in USD per tonne of CO2"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Development of carbon tax rates")
 

```

#PLotting fossil fuels share in the countries energy mix, and in a seperte plot emissions agains GDP.

```{r}
#| label: Fossil fuels share in energy mix agains emissions per capita
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 8

Final_dataset %>% #Putting the countries in order from highest to lowest e, and getting the average.
  mutate(Country = reorder(Country, Emissions_per_capita, FUN = mean)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Year, Country, size = Fossil_fuels_share, colour = Emissions_per_capita)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 1) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "paleturquoise", high = "midnightblue", breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 5), name = "Tonnes CO2e\nper person") +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 10), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10),
             name = "Fossil fuel\nshare (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2005, 2024, by = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right") +
  labs(title = "Emissions per Capita and Fossil Fuel Dependence")
  
```

```{r}
#| label: GDP per capita agains emissions per capita
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 8

#Order of countries by average emissions (lowest at bottom, highest at top)
Final_dataset %>% 
  mutate(Country = reorder(Country, Emissions_per_capita, FUN = mean)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Year, Country, size = GDP_per_capita, colour = Emissions_per_capita)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 5) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "lightblue1", high = "midnightblue", breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 5), name = "Tonnes CO2e\nper person") +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 10), breaks = c(10000, 20000, 40000, 60000, 80000, 110000), labels = scales::label_comma(),
             name = "GDP per capita") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2005, 2024, by = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right") +
  labs(title = "GDP and emissions per capita")

```
